1.9 Integrated Management of Public

Distribution System (IM-PDS)

The Government have issued orders to

implement Integrated Management of Public

26

Distribution System (IM-PDS) in the State. One

Nation One Ration Card Scheme (ONORC) has

been implemented in Tamil Nadu since October

2020. This enables Priority Households to procure

entitled commodities from any other State by

using Biometric Aadhaar authentication. Through

this scheme the other State people can lift the

commodities paying appropriate price.

1.10 Corona Relief Measures

1.10.1 Distribution of Corona

Relief Fund

To mitigate the livelihood loss of the common

people due to corona pandemic, an amount of

Rs.8,392.76 Crore has been distributed as corona

cash relief support @ Rs.4000/- in two

instalments of Rs.2000/- each (May and June

2021) to 2,09,81,900 rice cardholders. 99.2% of

the rice cardholders availed the cash relief.

27

1.10.2 Distribution of Grocery Kit

As part of corona relief, kit containing 14

grocery items were distributed to all the rice

1.10.4 Supply of Rice under Pradhan Mantri

Scheme at Free of Cost

In view of Covid-19 Pandemic Government

of India has allocated additional rice at the rate of

5 kg per person for the month of May and June

2021 for the Priority Household (PHH) and Priority

Household–Antyodaya Anna Yojana (PHH–AAY)

under Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana

(PMGKAY) scheme. To mitigate the difficult

situation being faced by the people in the

wake of the pandemic and the lockdown,

Government have issued orders sanctioning a

sum of Rs.687.84 Crore from the State Fund to

allocate 5 kg of rice per beneficiary to the

99,86,457 Non Priority Household rice cardholders

for the months of May and June 2021.

30

1.11 Food Subsidy

The Government of Tamil Nadu is following

Universal Public Distribution System ensuring and

realizing the goal of food security to all citizens of

the State. The State bears huge expenditure

towards subsidy for procurement and supply of

essential commodities under Public Distribution

System (especially foodgrains such as rice and

wheat are supplied free of cost) as well as Special

Public Distribution System Tur Dal and Palmolein

Oil to the family cardholders. In the Budget

Estimate 2021-22, the Government have allotted

a sum of Rs.8,437.57 Crore to meet the Food

Subsidy for effective implementation of the Public

Distribution System in the State.

31

Chapter - 2

CONSUMER PROTECTION

The prime objective of the Consumer

Protection policy of Government is to ensure that

Goods and Services are available at fair prices

and with good quality. It aims towards protecting

the consumers from the changing technology and

the impact of Globalization and Digitization in

trade. For this, necessary fair trade practices are

identified and regulated in order to prevent

consumers from exploitation of any kind.

The Government is carrying out following

activities to ensure wellbeing of the consumers in

Tamil Nadu.

1. Continuously providing awareness to the

Consumers regarding their rights under the

purview of Consumer Protection Act, 2019

and their responsibilities as empowered

Consumers.

32

2. Protecting Consumers from exploitation

through alternative Consumers Dispute

Redressal Mechanism which help consumers

to get resolved their disputes even without

approaching Consumer Disputes Redressal

5. As the costing is only a tentative cost, the initial sanction has been limited to Rs.400/- per kit in anticipation of savings on selected items in the actual bidding. Further it is considered appropriate that, funds are released from Demand No.51 under Major Head “2945” as this is an item of COVID relief and eligible under SDRF as gratuitous immediate relief. Pending presentation of the main Budget 2021-2022, the requisite expenditure can initially be met from an advance from the Food Subsidy intended for the 2"? quarter of 2021-2022.

6. The Government after careful consideration pass the following orders:-

(i) A sum of Rs.844.51 crore (Rupees eight hundred and forty four crore and fifty one lakh only) (2,11,12,798 X Rs.400 = Rs.844,51,19,200) is sanctioned and released immediately to the Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation to enable the Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation to procure and distribute 2,11,12,798 Grocery kits (details of items per kit as annexed) to the Rice Family Cardholders as a relief measure during corona pandemic, by relaxing Quarterly Control of Appropriation system for which orders were issued in the Government Letter No.15417/Fin(BG-l)Dept./2021-1, dated 30.03.2021. Further, this QCA relaxation is included in the online Quarterly Control of Appropriation (QCA) module of IFHRMS also, to facilitate drawal bills under IFHRMS as well.

(ii) Permission to the Managing Director, Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation to float short term tender for the procurement of commodities for Grocery items during this Covid pandemic emergency situation.

(iii) Release of funds from Demand No.51 under Major Head “2245” as this is an item of COVID relief and eligible under SDRF as gratuitous immediate relief. A specific inclusion within these norms should be taken up by Revenue Department as this is an unprecedented calamity.

(iv) Pending presentation of the main Budget 2021-2022, the requisite expenditure shall be initially met from an advance from the Food Subsidy intended for the 2" quarter of 2021-2022

4. From the Managing Director, Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation, Chennai-10 Letter No.BS6/13913/2021, dated 11.05.2021.

2. From the Commissioner of Civil Supplies and Consumer Protection, Letter No.E2/9925/2021, dated 12.05.2021.

ORDER:-

The Government of Tamil Nadu has announced complete lockdown in the State from 10.05.2021 to 24.05.2021 in view of Covid pandemic situation. In the letter first read above, the Managing Director, Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation has stated that, in the meeting chaired by the Hon'ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu on 11.05.2021, it has been decided to distribute 14 grocery items with cloth bag to the Rice Family Cardholders, in order to secure the livelihood of the people affected during Covid pandemic situation.

2. In this regard, the Managing Director, Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation has informed that, as per the decision taken in the meeting, for the distribution of 14 grocery items, such as, Wheat Flour, Salt, Rava, Sugar, Urad Dhal, Tamarind, etc., at an estimated cost of Rs.412.33 each to the 2,07,66,950 numbers of Rice Family Cardholders, a sum of Rs.856.28 crore is required. The Managing Director, Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation has stated that, the above expenditure may vary after finalization of the tender to be floated by the TNCSC by following due procedures laid down in the Tamil Nadu Transparency in Tenders Act, 4998 and Rules 2000 for the purchase of the above commodities.

3. The Managing Director, Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation has requested to sanction and release a sum of Rs.856.28 crore (Rupees eight hundred and fifty six crore and twenty eight lakh) immediately to the Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation to enable the Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation to procure and speedy distribution of Grocery items to the Rice Family Cardholders. Further, the Managing Director, Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation has informed that, instead of adopting clause-16(a) of Tamil Nadu Transparency in Tenders Act, 4998 for the procurement of commodities by Tamil Nadu

2

Civil Supplies Corporation during this Covid pandemic emergency situation, TNCSC proposes to float short term tender to ensure transparency in procuring the commodities for Covid relief works.

4. In the letter second read above, the Commissioner of Civil Supplies and Consumer Protection has reported that, 2,15,00,062 Family Cards are in circulation. Out of which 2,11,12,798 Family Cards are Rice Family Cards (including Srilankan Refugees). The Commissioner of Civil Supplies and Consumer Protection has requested release of funds for the distribution of Grocery items under the head of Relief Measures for Disaster Management.
